newsitem.title: USA: CBOT March soymeal sets contract high, oil ends up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT March soymeal sets contract high, oil ends up.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended sharply higher and a contract high was notched in the March on fund and commercial buying, traders said.
Soyoil futures also closed higher on spillover support from strong gains in soymeal and soybeans.
"Funds bought at least 1,200 March meal and put in new highs," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

March soymeal peaked at $260 per ton, eclipsing the previous high of $258.00 set on September 11. The floor had been waiting the move allsession after the March toyed with contract highs on Wednesday but failed to reach them.
The market rallied in spite of Thursday's U.S. Census Bureau data which showed December and January crushing rates were at two-year highs, meaning large amounts of soy products.

The report confirmed soymeal and soyoil stockpiles grew in January. Soymeal stocks were at 213,566 tons, up from 200,880 tons in December. Soyoil stocks climbed to 2.169 billion lbs from 2.027 billion in December.
Soymeal ended $6.00 to $2.00 a ton higher with March up $6.00 at $259.40.
Soyoil closed 0.33 to 0.20 cent per lb higher with March up 0.29 at 24.01.
Talk of possible shipping delays in Brazil lent support.
Brazilian sources said earlier this week several vessels were waiting to load soymeal at Parana state's Paranagua port and unsettled weather could further delay shipments.
Brazil was expected to harvest a record large crop but U.S. traders said that was irrelevant if Brazil could not get the supplies to the ports.
Technically, both markets posted impressive gains with the March soyoil contract holding above 24.00 cents per lb, a key technical point, traders said.
On the day, SAK Futures bought 600 lots March and 200 lots May soymeal, floor sources said. Cargill Inc bought 200 lots March and 100 May and Continental Grain bought 200 March.
In soyoil, Rosenthal Collins bought 1,000 lots May, Tenco Inc bought 500 March and Griffin Trading and Produce Grain each bought 300 May, traders said. ADM bought 500 March but sold 800 May.

Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 27,000 lots, against Wednesday's actual volume of 31,269 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 25,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 23,605 lots, CBOT reported.
